findings.evidence: Isometry.lean:414-418; the only use is line 458. `LinearMap.coe_equivOfIsUnitDet` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Determinant.lean:560) and `LinearMap.isUnit_iff_isUnit_det` (ibid.:327) give bijectivity from `IsUnit f.det` alone under `[Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M]`.
findings.fix: Drop `hf` and the isometry namespace: state `theorem bijective_of_isUnit_det (hdet : IsUnit (LinearMap.det f)) : Function.Bijective f`, proved by `LinearMap.coe_equivOfIsUnitDet hdet ▸ (LinearMap.equivOfIsUnitDet hdet).bijective` (or via Mathlib's `LinearMap.isUnit_iff_isUnit_det`), and have `IsIsometry.bijective` (line 457) call it with `hf.isUnit_det_of_nondegenerate hB`.
findings.issue: `IsIsometry.bijective_of_isUnit_det (hf : IsIsometry B f) (hdet : IsUnit (LinearMap.det f)) : Function.Bijective f` has `hf` (and hence `B`) entirely unused: the conclusion never mentions `B`, and the proof only uses `hf` to build `toIsometryGroupOfIsUnitDet`, whose underlying map is `LinearMap.equivOfIsUnitDet hdet`. Its own docstring states the form-free fact ("An endomorphism of a finite free module with unit determinant is bijective"). Placing it in the `IsIsometry` namespace makes a general fact look form-dependent.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/GeneralLinearGroup/Basic.lean:30 (`variable [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]`) covers `generalLinearEquiv` (:83), and `congrLinearEquiv` (:110) sits under `[Semiring R₁] [Semiring R₂]` (:98-106), even semilinearly.
findings.fix: Weaken the variable line to `[Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M₁] [Module R M₁] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [Module R M₂]`; the existing proofs (`congrLinearEquiv_apply`, `coeFn_generalLinearEquiv`, `coe_ofLinearEquiv`, `apply_symm_apply`) go through unchanged.
findings.issue: `TauCeti.LinearEquiv.congrAut` and its two evaluation lemmas assume `[CommSemiring R]`, but nothing in the definition or the proofs uses commutativity; every Mathlib ingredient is stated at `Semiring`. This is a general-purpose GL infrastructure file, so the extra hypothesis blocks non-commutative consumers for no reason.

summary: Two too-strong hypotheses remain: `IsIsometry.bijective_of_isUnit_det` carries an isometry hypothesis its statement never uses, and the new shared `LinearEquiv.congrAut` demands `CommSemiring R` where Mathlib's ingredients need only `Semiring R`. The prior round's `CommRing`/`AddCommGroup` over-restriction is fixed.
